Based on my search, here are the typical jersey numbers for linebackers in football:

## NFL Linebacker Jersey Numbers

### Traditional Rules (Pre-2021)
Under the long-standing NFL numbering system, linebackers were required to wear:
- **Primary:** 50–59
- **Alternate:** 90–99 (if 50-59 were unavailable)

This system was first standardized in 1973, with linebackers allowed to wear 90-99 added in 1984, and 40-49 allowed starting in 2015.

### Current Rules (2021 and beyond)
After the NFL expanded jersey number rules in 2021 (and further in 2023), linebackers can now wear:
- **0–59** and **90–99**

This significant expansion allows linebackers to wear single-digit numbers, numbers in the teens, 20s, 30s, and 40s, in addition to the traditional 50s and 90s.

### Historical Context
The numbering system originated from football's early days when players played both offense and defense. Fullbacks often played linebacker and wore numbers in the 30s, while centers and guards who played linebacker wore numbers in the 50s and 60s. As the game evolved and positions became specialized, the numbering system was formalized to help identify positions on the field.

### College Football
College football has traditionally had more flexible numbering rules than the NFL. The only strict requirement is that offensive linemen in ineligible positions must wear 50-79. While many college linebackers follow similar conventions to the NFL (wearing 40-59 and 90-99), there is more flexibility, and duplicate numbers are allowed as long as both players aren't on the field at the same time.

### Notable Impact
The 2021 rule change was notable enough that Tom Brady publicly criticized it, arguing that the expanded number ranges would make it harder for quarterbacks to identify defensive personnel and matchups before the snap, as linebackers could now wear numbers that previously indicated skill positions or defensive backs.

4. https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Squad_number
5. https://www.nfl-therapy.com/2021/02/football-101-glossary-nfl.html
6. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Number_(sports)
